Meet the couple raising their son in the woods to ‘set him up for strong independence as an adult’

27 Shares
by Dollita Okine, 8:00am August 09, 2026,
  • 27 Shares
  • Shares
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:05
Instaread

Brianne and Julius Bailey have chosen to raise their son in the woods. While most 3-year-olds spend their afternoons bouncing between toys, television, and tablets, their son spends a typical day wandering through the woods, learning about wild plants, and finishing the day with his family.

The couple shared a glimpse of their off-grid life on TikTok, and netizens were captivated by the barefoot child playing out alongside the home they built by hand. 

But Brianne and Julius told People that their lifestyle has never been about running away from contemporary life. It’s about being intentional with the one they’re building for their son.

Though they do not believe families must live off the grid to be close to God, they said they feel called to this way of life.

READ ALSO: Viral parents explain why their six children all have names starting with ‘Cam’ amid backlash

“Yahuah (God) is the guiding light of our lives and central to everything we do,” they remarked.

Each day starts with family and faith, transitioning into outdoor adventures. 

“A typical day for our child includes lots of hands-on learning and freedom to experience and grow,” they explained.

That routine includes family Bible readings, visits with grandparents, cousins, and friends, and hours of intuitive play in the nearby woods. These encounters inevitably turn into biology, botany, and zoology lessons, providing their son with an education they feel goes well beyond a classroom.

“This enables him to blossom in a more independent way,” the parents noted. “We believe that will set him up for strong independence as an adult.”

The couple revealed that one of the biggest misconceptions they face is that raising a child off the grid means sacrificing comfort or convenience, despite the fact that many people believe this. They just decide when and how it fits into their family’s life; they aren’t actually against modern technology.

READ ALSO: Mom distributes free special door locks to community to keep children with autism safe from wandering

They stated, “We don’t find our lifestyle inconvenient.” Rather, they describe their strategy as deliberate, pointing out the fact that their son isn’t “glued to an iPad screen or the constant light of a smartphone” and spends a lot more time outside than the typical child.

Their approach also influences how they juggle parenting and work. Their weeks typically involve business duties, property projects, and content creation. Yet, they emphasize that family always comes first, dedicating every Saturday as a day of rest free from work or business commitments.

Every choice they make as parents is still heavily influenced by their faith. They say they want to set an example for their son as he grows up by keeping the Sabbath, celebrating biblical feast days, and making an effort to love their neighbors.

Brianne and Julius hope that as their son gets older, he will maintain the same level of independence and curiosity that formed his early years. They know that in the end, his future will be his, but one part of theirs remains the same.

They remarked, “We have the home and the land and the well. Why would we give all that up just to go back to being more reliant on someone else? We are off-grid for keeps.”
